messages:
nina: quick heads-up: found a hang when cancelling a generator stream in the Go SDK (v0.9.1). short repro below.

nina: repro:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
gen := client.Generator("small-gen")
stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, &redwood.GenerateOptions{MaxTokens: 500})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

go func() {
  time.Sleep(120 * time.Millisecond)
  cancel()
}()

for {
  tok, err := stream.Next()
  if err != nil {
    log.Println("ended:", err)
    break
  }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
// observed: loop never breaks after cancel, goroutine sticks
```

omar: thanks nina. did you try forcing a Close on the response body? I think stream type in 0.9.1 lacks Close(), so callers can't.

nina: right, no Close(). also confirmed the underlying TCP connection stays open after cancel.

tj: this matches a pattern where Next() does a blocking read without selecting on ctx.Done(). we should: (1) ensure http.Request uses ctx (it does), (2) add stream.Close() to close resp.Body, (3) make Next() return ctx.Err() when ctx canceled.

omar: agree. parity note: python/js SDKs expose stream.close() and iterator throws Cancelled. Go should match ergonomics.

devex-bot: label added: go-sdk:stream-cancel

nina: i'll open a minimal PR with Close() and a unit test that cancels the context and asserts Next() unblocks.

tj: also add a short quickstart snippet recommending `defer stream.Close()`.

omar: if PR merges quickly, we can cut 0.9.2 patch release. impact seems medium (leaked goroutines for streaming users).

nina: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-redwood/pull/427 (wip)

devex-bot: CI queued for PR #427

nina: local tests passing; CI green. merging shortly.

devex-bot: merged commit 2b7e4a  go-redwood v0.9.2-rc1

nina: confirmed repro fixed on my machine; Next() returns context.Canceled and loop exits. closing thread.
